memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'When a woman has a discharge of blood for many days at a time other than her monthly period or has a discharge that continues beyond her period, she will be unclean as long as she has the discharge, just as in the days of her period. Any bed she lies on while her discharge continues will be unclean, as is her bed during her monthly period, and anything she sits on will be unclean, as during her period.'" - Lev 15:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is her verse. The woman in Mark's Gospel who had been bleeding for twelve years lived under exactly this law.

Read it again with her in mind. Unclean as long as she has the discharge. Not seven days — twelve years. Every bed. Every chair. Twelve years without a normal embrace, without entering the temple courts, without sitting where others sat. Mark adds that she had spent everything she had on doctors and had only grown worse (Mark 5:26).

Then she heard about Jesus. And she made a decision that broke every rule in this chapter — she pushed through a crowd, touching people as she went, and took hold of His cloak.

By the logic of Leviticus, she had just made Jesus unclean.

But that is not what happened. Immediately her bleeding stopped (Mark 5:29). The flow went the other way. Where the law said uncleanness spreads to whatever it touches, Jesus reversed the current entirely. Holiness moved out from Him and healed her.

Then He called her Daughter, and said: your faith has healed you. Go in peace (Mark 5:34).

Twelve years of isolation ended in a word. If you have been waiting a long time, He is not put off by how long it has been.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have you been carrying for years without relief?
2. What would it look like to reach out to Jesus in the middle of it?
3. How does it change things that holiness flows out from Christ to you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that when the desperate woman touched You, cleansing flowed out to her. I reach out to You today with what I have carried too long. Amen.
